papers.reason: This paper presents multi-epoch broadband X-ray spectral and timing observations of the atoll-type neutron star low-mass X-ray binary GX 9+9, placing quantitative physical constraints on the boundary layer size, accretion disk truncation, and compact object magnetic field.

papers.title: Fast radio bursts track cosmic star formation history with time delay: the effect of burst fluence
papers.result: When marginalizing over fluence calibration systematics and fitting the dispersion measure ($\mathrm{DM}$) distribution alone, both CHIME catalogs reveal a significant cosmological time delay: Catalog 1 yields $t_{d}=3.90^{+0.50}_{-0.41}\mathrm{~Gyr}$ with $\sigma_{t_{d}}=1.99^{+0.01}_{-0.24}\mathrm{~Gyr}$, while Catalog 2 yields $t_{d}=3.53^{+0.11}_{-0.10}\mathrm{~Gyr}$ with $\sigma_{t_{d}}=1.82^{+0.15}_{-0.14}\mathrm{~Gyr}$, resolving the apparent $t_d \sim 0$ result that arises from instrumental $\mathrm{S/N}$--fluence mapping biases.
papers.problem: Whether FRB occurrence rates follow prompt core-collapse supernova magnetar channels or delayed compact binary mergers, and how systematic uncertainties in telescope beam attenuation and fluence threshold mapping bias delay time inference in forward modeling.
papers.method: Forward modeling using a two-dimensional binning scheme over $\mathrm{S/N}$ and $\mathrm{DM}$ with synthetic injection samples, Poisson likelihood $\ln\mathcal{L}\propto\sum_{i,j}[n_{ij}\ln\zeta_{ij}-\zeta_{ij}]$, and an intrinsic burst energy distribution parameterized by a Schechter function $P(E)\propto\frac{1}{E_{\mathrm{char}}}\left(\frac{E}{E_{\mathrm{char}}}\right)^{\gamma}\exp\left(-\frac{E}{E_{\mathrm{char}}}\right)$ convolved with cosmic SFR and Gaussian DTD.
papers.reason: This work directly addresses the progenitor channels of fast radio bursts (FRBs) by testing whether FRBs track cosmic star formation history promptly or with a multi-gigayear delay time distribution.

papers.title: An oxygen-rich supernova remnant in NGC 253 with narrow [N II] emission lines
papers.result: Identified SNR 253-A in NGC 253 featuring broad $[\mathrm{O\,III}]\lambda 5007$ with two main components having $\mathrm{FWHM} = 1570\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ and $1760\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ (reverse shock heating fast ejecta), contrasted with narrow $[\mathrm{N\,II}]\lambda\lambda 6548, 6583$ with $v \approx 229\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ from circumstellar medium. Chandra counterpart 2CXO J004749.0-251628 yields $L_{\rm X} = 4.1_{-1.3}^{+1.2} \times 10^{36}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$, while $[\mathrm{O\,III}]$ luminosity is $\sim 5$ times Cas A. JWST limits constrain dust mass to $M_{\rm dust} \lesssim 10^{-4}\,M_\odot$ at $T_{\rm dust} = 120\,\mathrm{K}$.
papers.problem: The physical origin and shock geometry underlying the dramatic linewidth discrepancy between fast-moving oxygen ejecta and narrow circumstellar nitrogen emission in young oxygen-rich supernova remnants.
papers.method: VLT/MUSE integral field spectroscopy ($4650\text{--}9350\,\mathrm{\AA}$) continuum-subtracted emission-line imaging combined with multi-component Gaussian fitting, cross-matched with archival HST/ACS, Chandra X-ray, and JWST/MIRI photometry.
papers.reason: This work identifies the first oxygen-rich supernova remnant in NGC 253 with distinct broad [O III] and narrow [N II] lines, constraining ejecta-circumstellar medium interaction and shock structures.

papers.title: Evolutionary Map of the Universe (EMU): the fraction of radio-detected quasi-stellar objects at high redshift
papers.result: EMU detects $124/808$ ($15\%$) of $z \ge 4$ QSOs, with detection fractions rising to $\sim 37\%$ at the optically bright end ($\mathrm{mag}_{\rm drop} \sim 18$). The radio-loud fraction ($R > 10$) remains stable at $8 \pm 1\%$. High radio powers of $P_{5\,\mathrm{GHz}} = 5\times 10^{24}\text{--}5\times 10^{27}\,\mathrm{W}\,\mathrm{Hz}^{-1}$ demonstrate that many formally radio-quiet sources are misaligned jetted systems viewed at angles $\theta \sim 20^\circ\text{--}40^\circ$, including rare candidate blazars at $z > 6$ with $R > 300$.
papers.problem: Investigating whether high-redshift radio-quiet ($R < 10$) QSOs genuinely lack relativistic jets or if traditional radio loudness criteria fail due to Doppler de-beaming and suppressed extended lobe emission in the early Universe.
papers.method: Cross-matching $808$ optically confirmed $z \ge 4$ QSOs with ASKAP EMU survey data at $0.943\,\mathrm{GHz}$ using a $6.4''$ positional tolerance. Relativistic beaming is modeled as $P^{\rm jet}_{5{\rm GHz}}(\theta) = \mathcal{P}^{\rm jet}_{5{\rm GHz}}\delta^p(\theta)$ with Doppler factor $\delta(\theta) = [\Gamma(1 - \beta\cos\theta)]^{-1}$ ($p = 3.3$, $\Gamma = 10$), predicting radio loudness $R(\theta) = R(0)[(\delta^p(\theta) + 1/f_5)/(\delta^p(0) + 1/f_5)]$ where $f_5 = \mathcal{P}^{\rm jet}_{5{\rm GHz}} / \mathcal{P}^{\rm ext}_{5{\rm GHz}} \sim 0.1\text{--}1$.
papers.reason: This survey paper provides empirical constraints on the occurrence and physics of relativistic jets in high-redshift ($z \ge 4$) QSOs using EMU radio data, testing orientation and Doppler beaming models.

papers.title: Lower Bound on the Lightest Neutrino Mass with Resonant Neutrino Self-Interactions
papers.problem: Setting a lower bound on the lightest neutrino mass $m_{\rm lightest}$, which currently only possesses upper bounds from terrestrial decay experiments and cosmology, by testing $s$-channel resonant scattering against relic neutrinos.
papers.reason: The paper investigates resonant neutrino self-interactions ($\nu$SI) between ultra-high-energy (UHE) astrophysical neutrinos and the cosmic neutrino background (C$\nu$B), presenting a novel astrophysical method to constrain the absolute neutrino mass scale.

papers.title: High-energy Electron Transport with Discrete Inverse Compton Scatterings
papers.result: Discrete Klein–Nishina scatterings produce a hard high-energy tail in the electron spectrum and alter spatial propagation scales; for the Geminga pulsar halo with injection index $\alpha = 2.24$ and magnetic field $B = 3\,\mu\mathrm{G}$, discrete scattering leads to a $\sim 15\%$ shift in the derived diffusion coefficient $D_0$ and conversion efficiency $\eta = 0.0404$ compared to continuous loss models.
papers.problem: Investigates the failure of the continuous energy loss approximation for ultra-high-energy electrons ($E_e \sim 100\,\mathrm{TeV}$) in the Klein–Nishina regime where discrete, stochastic inverse Compton scatterings with CMB photons cause large fractional energy losses (up to $\sim 50\%$) per collision, modifying spectral shapes and spatial halo profiles.
papers.method: Constructs an integro-differential transport equation $\frac{\partial N}{\partial t} = D_\parallel(E)\frac{\partial^2 N}{\partial r_\parallel^2} + D_\perp(E)\nabla_\perp^2 N - \nu(E)N + \int_E^{E_{\rm max}} T(E, E')N(E')\,{\rm d}E'$, discretizes it on a logarithmic energy grid into matrix form $[s\mathbf{I} + \mathbf{A} + q^2\mathbf{F}]\widetilde{\widehat{\mathbf{N}}}(q,s) = \mathbf{Q}(s)$, and solves it analytically in Fourier space followed by Talbot contour numerical inverse Laplace transformation.
papers.reason: The paper develops an exact semi-analytical Fourier–Laplace transform framework with a Talbot contour to solve the electron transport equation under discrete Klein–Nishina inverse Compton scattering, offering a deterministic alternative to Monte Carlo simulations for compact object high-energy halos.

papers.title: Optical Light-Curve Broadening in the Redback Binary PSR J2215+5135
papers.result: Between 2014 and 2024, the optical light-curve wings broadened significantly (at $4.26\sigma$ significance via permutation test) while peak brightness and orbital phase remained constant. Light-curve modeling yields an inferred neutron-star mass of $M_{\mathrm{NS}} = 1.95^{+0.11}_{-0.07}\,M_\odot$ for 2024 (consistent within $\sim 1\sigma$ of $2.13^{+0.16}_{-0.13}\,M_\odot$ in 2014) with heating efficiency $L_{\mathrm{X}}/\dot{E} = 0.95^{+0.24}_{-0.10} \approx 1$ relative to spin-down luminosity $\dot{E} = 5.29\times 10^{34}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$, mass ratio $q = 0.144\pm 0.009$, and inclination $i = 68.05^{\circ}\pm 1.26^{\circ}$.
papers.problem: Whether secular companion surface temperature changes and light-curve morphology variations over a decadal baseline create systematic biases in spider pulsar irradiation modeling and neutron-star mass determination.
papers.method: Multicolor $g^{\prime}, r^{\prime}, i^{\prime}$ light curves from the INO 3.4 m telescope modeled using the ELC code with Roche geometry, gravity darkening ($T_{\mathrm{eff}} \propto g^{\beta}$ with $\beta = 0.1$), limb darkening, NextGen/Kurucz atmospheres, and MCMC parameter exploration.
papers.reason: This paper investigates optical light-curve broadening and companion surface heating evolution in the redback millisecond pulsar PSR J2215+5135, quantifying systematic uncertainties in massive neutron-star mass measurements.

papers.title: Clouds as near-horizon backgrounds in the radio detection of air showers
papers.result: Under bistatic forward-scattering geometry at grazing elevation ($\epsilon = 5^\circ$, bistatic angle $\theta = 170^\circ$), the simulated peak instantaneous radar cross section of a cloud reaches $\sigma \sim 0.1\ \mathrm{m}^2$ ($-10\ \mathrm{dBsm}$), demonstrating that cloud reflection of ground-based transmitters can produce detectable near-horizon pulses.
papers.problem: Radio detection of cosmic rays and ultra-high-energy neutrinos is contaminated by sporadic, near-horizon ($10^\circ\text{--}20^\circ$ elevation) radio frequency interference (RFI) that cannot be eliminated by conventional horizon cuts.
papers.method: The study develops a passive radar scattering framework (MARES), dividing a cloud into cubic cells of size $L_c \simeq 1.6d$ with Gaussian positional jitter $\delta = L_c/3$ to suppress artificial Bragg resonances, and computes single-droplet Rayleigh scattering (dielectric factor $|K_{\mathrm{water}}|^2 \approx 0.93$) and coherent cell radar cross section (RCS).
papers.reason: This paper investigates unexplained near-horizon RFI observed in air shower radio arrays (e.g., AERA, OVRO-LWA, BEACON, GRAND), proposing cloud reflections of anthropogenic emissions as the underlying physical mechanism.

papers.title: A Chandra X-Ray Survey of the Middle-aged Supernova Remnant G22.7-0.2 Interacting with Molecular Clouds
papers.result: Chandra ACIS-I PSF modeling and deconvolution resolve spatial extension in CCC candidates at $d \sim 4.4\text{--}4.7\ \mathrm{kpc}$: N2 displays significant extension with $R_{90} = 2.35^{\prime\prime}$ (physical radius $r \sim 0.052\pm 0.002\ \mathrm{pc}$), N1 exhibits marginal extension with $R_{90} = 0.82^{\prime\prime}$ ($r \sim 0.018\pm 0.0006\ \mathrm{pc}$), while N3 is point-like ($R_{90} = 0.31^{\prime\prime}$). N2's hard spectrum (photon index $\Gamma = 1.2^{+0.4}_{-0.4}$) and uniform-sphere mass ($M \approx 0.6\ M_\odot$ at shock-compressed density $n_{\mathrm{H}} \sim 3\times 10^4\ \mathrm{cm}^{-3}$) match non-thermal bremsstrahlung (NTB, predicted $\Gamma \simeq 1$), whereas N1 ($\\Gamma = 2.1^{+0.5}_{-0.4}$, $M \approx 0.03\ M_\odot$) favors a high-density synchrotron hot spot.
papers.problem: Observational constraints on the cloud clump mass function (CMF, $\mathrm{d}N/\mathrm{d}\ln M \propto M^{-\alpha}$) at the theoretical minimum scale $r \sim 0.01\text{--}0.1\ \mathrm{pc}$ have been lacking due to spatial resolution limits, leaving the spatial extent and dominant non-thermal emission mechanism (synchrotron vs. non-thermal bremsstrahlung) of hard X-ray ($>10\ \mathrm{keV}$) sources in middle-aged SNRs unresolved.
papers.method: Analyzed Chandra ACIS-I observations ($58.05\ \mathrm{ks}$ total exposure) using `wavdetect` in $0.5\text{--}7.0\ \mathrm{keV}$, simulated local PSFs via ChaRT v2 and MARX 5.5.3 using absorbed power-law spectral models, fitted radial profiles with a Moffat function $\mathrm{Flux\ density} = \mathrm{ampl}\times [1 + ((x - x_{\mathrm{pos}})/r_0)^2]^{0.5 - 3\beta}$, deconvolved source radial models from PSF models to obtain the 90% encircled flux radius $R_{90}$, and modeled forward dust-scattering halos with differential cross-section $\frac{\mathrm{d}\sigma_{\mathrm{sca}}}{\mathrm{d}\Omega} \propto a^6 \exp[-0.4575 E^2 a^2 \theta_{\mathrm{sca}}^2]$.
papers.reason: This paper presents Chandra sub-arcsecond imaging of the middle-aged supernova remnant G22.7$-$0.2 interacting with molecular clouds, confirming spatial extension in crushed cloud clumps (CCCs) powered by non-thermal bremsstrahlung from low-energy cosmic rays.

papers.title: A search and multi-frequency study of curved parsec-scale jets in active galaxies
papers.result: Among 7,927 resolved AGN sources, 586 show reliable curvature with bending rate $|K|$ increasing at higher frequencies, tracing stronger deflection in the innermost jet. Linear helical modeling gives a mean curvature $K^{-1}_{\rm mean} = 109^{\circ}/{\rm mas}$, corresponding to inferred precession periods $P \sim 10\text{--}10^{4}~{\rm yr}$ (logarithmic mean $218.8~{\rm yr}$). For binary black hole models, disk tidal precession $P_{\rm td} \approx 6.5 \times 10^{2} M_{8} q^{-1} (r_{b}/10^{4} r_{g})^{3} (R_{d}/10^{4} r_{g})^{-3/2}~{\rm yr}$ matches observations much better than spin geodetic precession $P_{\rm geo} \approx 2.6 \times 10^{8} M_{8} q^{-1} (r_{b}/10^{4} r_{g})^{5/2}~{\rm yr}$, while tilted thick disc Lense-Thirring precession $P_{\rm BH, spin, thick} \approx 24.7 s^{-1} M_{8} (r_{\rm o}/100 r_{g})^{3} (r_{\rm o}/100 r_{\rm i})^{1/2}~{\rm yr}$ naturally reproduces the observed range of $10^{1\text{--}5}~{\rm yr}$.
papers.problem: Determining the physical origins of parsec-scale relativistic jet bending in active galaxies, specifically distinguishing between geometric precession (induced by supermassive binary black hole orbits or Bardeen-Petterson/Lense-Thirring disc warping) and plasma dynamical instabilities (Kelvin-Helmholtz helical modes).
papers.method: Filtered 123,456 Astrogeo VLBI images (1.2–86 GHz) down to 63,879 images of 7,927 resolved sources using 2D Gaussian subtraction with threshold $\sigma_{\rm crit} = 5.5\sigma_{\rm map}$. Identified curved jets via median ridge lines with $\Delta\phi = |K|(r_{\rm max} - r_{\rm min}) > 20^{\circ}$, then performed gradient-free global optimization fitting to linear helices (scaling parameter $K = \frac{1}{\pi}\frac{c}{d}\frac{\beta}{1-\beta}P\sin\psi$) and logarithmic helices ($K_{\rm log} = \frac{2\pi}{\tan\psi}[\frac{r_0}{\lambda_0}]$), inverting physical parameters through $10^4$ Monte Carlo draws from empirical prior distributions.
papers.reason: This paper presents a large-scale statistical identification and multi-frequency geometric modeling of 586 curved parsec-scale relativistic jets in AGN, providing systematic observational constraints on relativistic jet propagation, precession mechanisms, and supermassive black hole binary or accretion disc dynamics.

papers.title: An X-ray binary origin for the LHAASO peanut
papers.result: The LHAASO peanut can be modeled as a microquasar jet relic located at $d \approx 1.3\ \mathrm{kpc}$ ($z \approx -370\ \mathrm{pc}$ below the Galactic plane), powered by leptonic Klein-Nishina inverse Compton emission with an electron cutoff energy $E_{\rm cut}^e = 0.99\ \mathrm{PeV}$, magnetic field $B = 2.87\ \mu\mathrm{G}$, spectral index $\Gamma_e = 1.93$, injection timescale $t_{\rm inj} = 5 \times 10^3\ \mathrm{yr}$, and an electron Eddington fraction $\alpha_e = 9 \times 10^{-4}$, predicting a quiescent counterpart flux of $F_{2-10\,\mathrm{keV}} \approx 6 \times 10^{-15}\ \mathrm{erg\ cm^{-2}\ s^{-1}}$.
papers.problem: Accounting for the physical origin, particle acceleration, and asymmetric $0.45^\circ \times 4.6^\circ$ morphology of the high-latitude ($b \approx -17.5^\circ$) LHAASO peanut UHE source, where the offset millisecond pulsar MSP J0218+4232 requires unrealistically extreme anisotropic particle transport over $\sim 250\ \mathrm{pc}$.
papers.method: GAMERA-based leptonic one-zone inverse Compton modeling on ISRF and CMB target photon fields coupled with semi-relativistic jet advection ($v_{\rm jet} \gtrsim 0.1c$), where low ambient magnetic fields ($B \sim 1\text{--}3\ \mu\mathrm{G}$) yield electron cooling times $t_{\rm cool} \sim 10^4\ \mathrm{yr}$ at $1\ \mathrm{PeV}$ to enable extended spatial propagation.
papers.reason: This paper proposes a quiescent low-mass X-ray binary (LMXB) jet relic model to explain the origin and morphology of the ultra-high-energy LHAASO peanut source, offering an important relativistic jet PeVatron perspective for compact object astrophysics.

papers.title: X-ray Polarization of the Western Lobe of SS 433
papers.result: IXPE observations reveal non-detection of X-ray polarization in the western lobe of SS 433, with best-fit Stokes parameters $Q = -0.01 \pm 0.12$ and $U = 0.01 \pm 0.13$, equivalent to $\mathrm{PD} = 1.4\% \pm 12.5\%$ and a 99% confidence upper limit of $\mathrm{PD} < 32\%$. The polarization degree is significantly lower than that of the eastern lobe ($\mathrm{PD} \approx 49\%\text{--}50\%$) at 99.5% ($2.8\sigma$) confidence, despite both lobes having comparable non-thermal photon indices ($\Gamma \approx 1.6$) and magnetic field strengths ($B \approx 10\text{--}15\,\mu\mathrm{G}$).
papers.problem: Investigating whether the western lobe of SS 433 exhibits high X-ray polarization and ordered magnetic fields aligned with the jet direction, comparable to the eastern lobe where synchrotron emission shows high polarization and well-ordered magnetic fields.
papers.method: Weighted spectropolarimetric analysis combining spatial, spectral, and particle character weights using leakagelib in the $2\text{--}5.5\,\mathrm{keV}$ band on IXPE observations (exposure $> 9.6 \times 10^5\,\mathrm{s}$ per DU), accounting for Chandra-derived astrophysical background and unabsorbed power-law instrumental background ($\chi^2/\mathrm{dof} = 161/147$) with a $1/\mathrm{PD}$ prior to correct for Ricean bias.
papers.reason: This paper presents IXPE X-ray polarization constraints on the western lobe of microquasar SS 433, setting a 99% confidence upper limit of $\mathrm{PD} < 32\%$. This provides an observational limit on magnetic field ordering and jet-ambient medium interaction in relativistic jet systems.

papers.title: Determining the Spin-down of the White Dwarf in J191213.72-441045.1 using Optical Time-Series Photometry
papers.problem: Determining whether the multi-wavelength pulsed non-thermal emission of the white dwarf pulsar J1912-4410 is powered solely by rotational spin-down or assisted by accretion, and testing the viability of the unipolar synchronar magnetospheric interaction model.
papers.method: Multi-band ($u, g, r, i$) high-speed time-series photometry obtained with ULTRACAM over 28 nights was reduced with HiPERCAM. Pulse arrival times were derived via cross-correlation with a Gaussian template (optimal width $\sigma = 29.3\,\mathrm{s}$ in $g$). Orbital modulation and timing residuals were disentangled using a 10-term Fourier series and iteratively fitted to a quadratic ephemeris $T_{\rm max} = T_0 + P_{\rm spin} E + \frac{1}{2} P_{\rm spin} \dot{P}_{\rm spin} E^2$ with MCMC parameter estimation.
papers.reason: J1912-4410 is only the second known white dwarf pulsar, providing a critical laboratory to test compact object spin-down power and magnetospheric non-thermal emission mechanisms. Measuring its spin-down rate directly tests whether the system is purely rotationally powered or aided by accretion.

papers.title: Measuring the flavor composition of high-energy neutrinos from the Milky Way
papers.result: With eight neutrino telescopes, the source electron flavor fraction $f_{e,{\rm S}}$ for the inner Galactic plane can be measured to $27\%$ precision at $68\%$ C.L., distinguishing pion decay ($f_{e,{\rm S}}=1/3$) from muon damping ($f_{e,{\rm S}}=0$) and neutron decay ($f_{e,{\rm S}}=1$) at $>95\%$ C.L. In extragalactic sources, muon synchrotron cooling above $E_{c} \approx E_{c,\mu}/3$ with $E_{c,\mu} \simeq 6\times 10^{9}~{\rm GeV}\,(B/{\rm G})^{-1}$ can be detected at $\ge 3\sigma$ for $\bar{B} \gtrsim 11\text{ kG}$ ($5\sigma$ for $\bar{B} \gtrsim 22\text{ kG}$), while neutrino invisible decay lifetime-to-mass ratio can be probed up to $\tau/m \sim 1.5\times 10^4\text{ s eV}^{-1}$ at $2\sigma$.
papers.problem: High-energy neutrinos from the Milky Way have an unknown flavor composition $(f_{e}, f_{\mu}, f_{\tau})$ and production origin (diffuse interstellar $pp$ collisions versus unresolved discrete sources), and existing facilities lack the sensitivity to distinguish emission mechanisms, detect muon synchrotron cooling in magnetized environments, or constrain neutrino decay against extragalactic baselines.
papers.method: The analysis uses a frequentist profile likelihood method based on Poisson event rates and Wilks' theorem across eight neutrino telescopes (IceCube, KM3NeT/ARCA, Baikal-GVD, P-ONE, TRIDENT, NEON, HUNT, IceCube-Gen2). The framework models detector tracks and cascades, computes atmospheric backgrounds using MCEq with Sibyll-2.3d and nuVeto self-veto, incorporates muon synchrotron cooling with critical cutoff $E_{c} \simeq 2\times 10^{9}~{\rm GeV}\,(B/{\rm G})^{-1}$, and folds in standard averaged neutrino oscillations $f_{\beta,\oplus} = \sum_{\alpha} P_{\alpha\beta} f_{\alpha,{\rm S}}$.
papers.reason: This paper presents observational sensitivity forecasts and theoretical frameworks for measuring the flavor composition of Galactic and extragalactic high-energy neutrinos using eight neutrino telescopes, enabling tests of cosmic-ray hadronic production mechanisms, source magnetic fields, and neutrino decay.
